papers.title: Attend Before Attention: Efficient and Scalable Video Understanding via Autoregressive Gazing
papers.authors: Baifeng Shi; Stephanie Fu; Long Lian; Hanrong Ye; David Eigen; Aaron Reite; Jan Kautz; Boyi Li; David M. Chan; Trevor Darrell; Pavlo Molchanov; Hongxu Yin

facts: Frames are encoded sequentially by a lightweight convolutional encoder; an autoregressive transformer decodes patch indices using current/past frames and prior selections.
Multi-scale vocabulary uses resolutions32,64,112,224 pixels in Fig.3. These are image scales, not four patch side lengths; author Appendix A says patch side16 and 265 candidate positions.

Decoder has patch-index prediction and reconstruction-loss prediction outputs. User threshold controls stopping per frame, then move to next frame; preserve autoregressive selected-index feedback/history.

Actual reconstruction model is custom block-causal VideoMAE used for objective/training reward. Predicted reconstruction loss, not rerunning actual reconstruction at each inference step, controls stopping.

Stage1 next-token-prediction learns from greedy-search gazing sequences, with auxiliary squared loss on reconstruction-loss prediction. Stage2 on-policy GRPO uses negative reconstruction reward and auxiliary loss prediction supervision.
Selected multi-scale patches are processed before downstream ViT, whose frame/position embeddings are interpolated per scale; tokens from16frames share a sequence and feed the MLLM.
Any-resolution/length inference tiles video into16×224×224 spatiotemporal blocks, runs gazing per tile, then merges positions.
Multi-token prediction uses several heads for multiple indices and corresponding losses; show it as an optional explicit inset/annotation, not replace history with fully parallel noncausal selection.
scientific: Current/past frame features and selected-patch history feed autoregressive decoding; no future-frame leakage arrow.
Multi-scale indices, their gathered patches, and actual image scales are distinct objects; scale labels do not falsely become patch side lengths.
Loss prediction head and user threshold drive per-frame stop/advance control, separate from patch-index data output.
Selected indices feed back as autoregressive history and advance-to-next-frame preserves past context.
Actual VideoMAE reconstruction/reward is training-only in the depicted training path; it is not falsely a mandatory downstream inference pass.
NTP→RL training sequence, reconstruction reward and loss-prediction supervision are represented with correct direction and boundaries.
Gazing selection precedes downstream ViT→MLLM; multi-scale embedding/position adaptation and tile/merge scope are explicit.
Multi-token prediction annotation retains causal history; caption states schematic redraw and does not claim original empirical speedups were reproduced.

papers.title: DOUBT: Decoupled Object-level Understanding and Bridging via vMF-based Trustworthiness for Hallucination Detection in MLLMs
papers.authors: Kaiqi Chen; Yang Qin; Changhao He; Xi Peng; Peng Hu
papers.read_scope: Sec.3 pp.3–5 in full, Fig.2 and Algorithm1 p.4, Eqs.1–6 p.4–5, implementation details p.6, stated object-error propagation p.4–5; conclusion and scope p.9–10. No claim of full24page deep reading.
papers.difficulty: Parallel sampling versus sequential object bridging; frozen sentence encoder; normalization/operator order; two-set score fusion; threshold polarity; reference-answer/evaluation isolation.
source_conflicts: PDF running title abbreviates the publication title; citation uses PMLR metadata.
The main prose sometimes calls scores uncertainty; Eq.5 and Algorithm1 clearly use high mean-resultant score as trustworthiness, flag1=non-hallucinatory.
The text labels the finite-sample resultant-length estimator unbiased; this property is not independently verified and must not be asserted by the redraw.

code.not_executed: GitHub tree request403rate limit. No retry or unpinned code claims; diagram grounded in official algorithm and equations.

facts: Input is image I and instruction/question t. Same black-box MLLM supplies a low-temperature reference answer A; this is an evaluated answer, not a score input.
Direct path samples K answers from M(I,t). Object path first recognizes up to3 main objects r=M(I,p_obj).
Bridging then samples K answers from M(I,t||p_bri||r), retaining image and original question, not only the object list.
Each response in each set is encoded by the same frozen nli-roberta-large sentence embedding model, then individually normalized to unit length.
For each set separately compute R_set=||sum_k e_hat_k||/K. Then R_avg=(R_ori+R_bri)/2; do not pool all2K vectors before norm.
R_avg>theta gives flag1, judged non-hallucinatory; R_avg≤theta gives flag0, hallucination. This is detection estimate, not truth guarantee.
Ground truth compares correctness of reference A against detection flag only in offline evaluation; no gold answers, retrieval database, gradient or fine-tuning required by detection diagram.

Reported setup K10, reference temperature0.1, sample temperature0.5, top-k10/top-p0.99, threshold0.48 are experimental choices, not universal architecture constants. Object-recognition errors may propagate.
scientific: Image plus original question reach both sampling paths; object recognition precedes bridging and supplies the object list only to the bridged path.
The same black-box MLLM and K-sample multiplicities are clear; object recognition is not depicted as K independent gold annotations.
Separate reference answer and offline correctness assessment are not score inputs or deployed ground truth.
Both paths use frozen sentence embeddings and per-response unit normalization before score computation.
Mean-resultant length is computed independently within each K-set; output operators show norm(mean vectors) then scalar average across sets, not pooled-vector norm or vote.
Threshold polarity and equality are correct: >theta→flag1 non-hallucinatory; ≤theta→flag0 hallucination.
No invented model-training, retrieval, learned detector or feedback correction loop; optional OUB correction discussion is not the detection pipeline.
Schematic caption states score is proxy, may fail after object misidentification; no claims that high consistency guarantees truth or published accuracy was reproduced.

facts: Two distinct input images use VAE image encoding; instruction is tokenized. Conditions are combined with timestep and separate noisy target latent for DiT, not pre-added pixel fusion.
Fig.3 p.5; Sec.III-A pp.4–5; code model.forward
Paper architecture uses32Transformer layers, pre-trained OmniGen/Phi3 base, LoRA adaptation; VAE remains frozen and trainable adaptations are distinguished from inference use.

Condition images are represented as visual tokens inside image delimiters; timestep token and noisy target tokens follow the condition sequence in inspected code. Output target tokens alone are converted back to latent image, then VAE decoder.

Hybrid attention is causal across sequence order but bidirectional inside an image block. Processor additionally allows output-image tokens to attend all earlier condition/time and own output tokens, never reverse future edges.
Training uses target x and noise epsilon to form x_t=t*x+(1-t)*epsilon; predict velocity and squared loss against x-epsilon. Target enters loss/noisy-target construction, not as inference input.
M3 duplicates a source image into two views, uses complementary corruption on75%patches and common corruption on25%, with noise-mask/Gaussian-noise/blur; target is original source forM3.
